clue.text: Union supporter surprisingly is left outside backing a communist

indicators.note: outside says the shuffled letters go around the other piece
surprisingly suggests the letters of is left turn up in an unexpected order
backing tells us to read a plus the word for communist from back to front

parts.note: a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A political observer is startled that a left-winger is endorsing a communist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' turns IS LEFT into FE...LIST, which goes 'outside' DERA, the result of 'backing' A RED.
explanation.definitionFit: A federalist supports a federal union of states, the stance of Hamilton and Madison in the Federalist Papers.

clue.text: Celebrity makes a couple of notes

parts.note: fa, the fourth note of the tonic sol-fa scale, is the first of the pair
me (or mi), the third sol-fa note, completes the couple of notes

explanation.surface: A star becomes famous after writing a couple of short messages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' looks like letters or memos, but they are musical notes of the sol-fa scale: FA followed by ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity as a state of being widely known is a straight synonym for renown.

clue.text: Deny Ovid was involved in Metamorphoses

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a change of form, so the letters of Ovid was change shape

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to believe the Roman poet Ovid had any part in writing his own Metamorphoses.
explanation.walkthrough: Metamorphoses really is Ovid's poem, which makes the surface plausible; here the word just signals the letters of OVID WAS changing form.
explanation.definitionFit: To disavow something is to refuse to acknowledge or own it, which is a way to deny it.

clue.text: Making a comeback, getting about in the pink?

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
a carnation is a pink, the garden flower of the Dianthus family

explanation.surface: Someone recovering their health is returning to action, back in the pink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the pink' looks like the idiom for healthy, but 'pink' is the flower, so IN + CARNATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is rebirth in a new body, a return to life, hence a comeback taken whimsically.

clue.text: Spare from socialist excess

parts.note: a socialist is on the political left
an amount over is an excess

explanation.surface: Something extra comes from a socialist's surplus.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective means remaining unused, surplus to what was needed.

clue.text: Posh part of London holding a mass for teacher

indicators.note: holding says the first piece contains the next ones

parts.note: SW1, read as SWI, is the postcode of Westminster and Belgravia, a wealthy part of London
m is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: An exclusive London district hosts a mass for a religious teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the London postcode covering Westminster and Belgravia; the figure 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu religious teacher or holy man.

clue.text: Theatrical party

definitions.meaning: exaggerated and showy in manner, an affected style
a group of people with a shared cause, as in the Remain side

explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes deliberately exaggerated, showy behaviour; a camp is also a faction holding a shared view.

clue.text: Swim over sea back to front, being fat

indicators.note: back to front says the last letter is taken from the back and put at the front

parts.note: to dip is to have a quick swim
o is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Swimming laps in the sea, then going the other way, while being overweight.
explanation.walkthrough: DIP + O + SEA gives DIPOSEA; 'back to front' moves its final A to the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose is the technical adjective for fatty tissue in the body.

clue.text: Lower orders comprehending students making fatuous remark

indicators.note: comprehending in its sense of including or taking in

parts.note: the peasantry are the poor rural working class
l for learner stands for a student, as on the L-plates of learner drivers

explanation.surface: Uneducated folk understanding pupils, then saying something silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehending' looks like understanding but means including: PEASANTRY takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasantry is a light joking comment of no real substance, a piece of polite small talk.

clue.text: Tangle with international footballer

parts.note: a tangle is a mess

explanation.surface: A defender gets in a tangle with an international footballer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'international footballer' reads as one phrase, but 'international' gives only the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Messi, the Argentine forward, is one of the most famous footballers of all time.

clue.text: Right to vote of a man in European country

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: France is a country of Europe
his means belonging to a man

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man living in another European country may vote.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the legal entitlement to cast a ballot, as in universal suffrage.

clue.text: One to welcome dawn crossing bridge with one's dog

indicators.note: crossing says the bird's letters stretch across the next pieces, holding them

parts.note: a cockerel crows at daybreak
a span is a bridge or its arch
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: An early riser crosses a bridge at dawn with their dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One to welcome dawn' is the crowing bird, and 'crossing' has it straddle the bridge and the one, so the bird's name is split around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The cocker spaniel is a popular breed of small gun dog with long ears.

clue.text: Award one successful with first clue!

parts.note: a victor is one who wins
1 Across is the first clue of a crossword, the figure read as I

explanation.surface: A prize for the first person to solve a puzzle's opening clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first clue' is 1 Across, written I ACROSS; the exclamation mark flags the self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest military decoration for gallantry.

clue.text: Alpine club disbanded is not to blame

indicators.note: a disbanded club breaks up, so its letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A mountaineering club that has broken up cannot be held responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: Inculpable means blameless, free of guilt; it is the negative of culpable.

clue.text: Crudely looks back on fresh depiction of recent events

indicators.note: on says the reversed piece is placed after the first

parts.note: fresh means new

indicators.note: back tells us to read that word from end to start

parts.note: to leer is to look at someone crudely

explanation.surface: Someone ogles a new film about current affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crudely looks' is a verb for ogling; 'back' turns it around, and 'on' places it after the word for fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsreel was a short cinema film reporting topical events, shown before the main feature.

clue.text: Lower status of church dignitary around Middle East

indicators.note: around says the dignitary goes about the region's letters

parts.note: a dean heads a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: Talk of a clergyman's reduced standing in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade them, to reduce their dignity or standing.

clue.text: Seized area captured by whirling Dervish

indicators.note: captured by says the letter is held within the other piece
whirling, like the dancing dervish, spins the letters around

explanation.surface: A spinning dervish, seized within a space, is captured in a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirling Dervish' looks like the familiar phrase, but 'whirling' shuffles DERVISH into RVISHED, which takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravished in its older sense means carried off by force, snatched.

clue.text: Cheerful pub to get drunk and have a meal

indicators.note: getting drunk muddles things, so the letters of pub stagger into a new order

parts.note: to eat is to have a meal

explanation.surface: A happy evening: go to the pub, have a few drinks, then dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat means optimistic and positive in mood.

clue.text: Headgear of daughter taken by one in hand

indicators.note: taken by says the letter is held inside the fruit

parts.note: a bunch of bananas is called a hand, so a banana is one in a hand

explanation.surface: A girl's headscarf held by someone's hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one in hand' seems to be anything held, but a hand is the name for a bunch of bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandana is a large coloured kerchief worn tied round the head.

clue.text: Product of Seagrams, one may relieve stress

indicators.note: a product is something made from raw material, so the letters of Seagrams are remade

explanation.surface: A drink from the Seagram distillery is touted as a way to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: Seagram's is a drinks company known for whisky and gin, which supports the surface about relaxing.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur or massage device kneads muscles to ease tension.

clue.text: Good family will take her to find London landmark

indicators.note: will take says the first pieces hold the next word

parts.note: kin means family

explanation.surface: A kind family will take a visitor to see a famous London sight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gherkin is the nickname of 30 St Mary Axe, a pickle-shaped skyscraper in the City of London.

clue.text: Biblical character — I put in 'apostle' erroneously

indicators.note: erroneously says the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly lists a Gospel figure among the twelve apostles.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea who sentenced Jesus in the Gospels.

clue.text: Will Shakespeare's first grand house

indicators.note: first says take just the opening letter of the playwright's name

parts.note: a hall is a large country house

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's first will left a grand house, recalling the famous second-best bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will Shakespeare' reads as the playwright's name, but Will is the definition, the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shall and will both express the future tense, as in 'I shall go'.

clue.text: Misdeeds regularly ignored in certain days in Rome

indicators.note: regularly ignored says every other letter of misdeeds is dropped

explanation.surface: Wrongdoings are routinely overlooked on certain dates in ancient Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell mid-month, the 15th of March, May, July and October and the 13th otherwise.

clue.text: Supporter at home was hard to indoctrinate

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means at home
h is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fan at home found it hard to convert others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' looks like a fan, but it is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainwash someone is to force beliefs on them, to indoctrinate them systematically.

clue.text: Head off arm-in-arm showing tattoos

indicators.note: head off says the first letter is cut away

parts.note: people arm-in-arm are linked

explanation.surface: A couple walking arm in arm show off their tattoos.
explanation.definitionFit: Inked is slang for tattooed, bearing ink designs on the skin.

clue.text: Dash around during vernal equinox

indicators.note: around says those letters are read from right to left
during says the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone rushes about at the spring equinox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' picks NALE from inside 'vernal equinox' and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash in the sense of flair and vigour, a stylish energy.

clue.text: Inexperienced people guided head of government in affairs

indicators.note: in says the pieces go inside the other

parts.note: flings are brief love affairs
led means guided

indicators.note: head of says take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Young politicians who led the government were caught in affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Fledglings are young birds just learning to fly, so figuratively novices or beginners.
